The only equivalence in play is clause (d) of the causal-response theorem quoted in [F9]; the forward direction, nonnegative work for every $e$ implies positive semidefiniteness of $M(\omega)$, is instantiated in step 4.1 in its failure form: the work is strictly negative for a nonzero $e$, so no nonnegative-work conclusion holds and $M(\omega)$ is not positive semidefinite.

The reverse direction of that equivalence, positive semidefiniteness implying nonnegative work, is not claimed here; step 4.1 uses the instantaneous formula $e^*M(\omega)e=|e|^2\operatorname{Im}\chi(\omega)<0$ directly, which witnesses the failure of the hypothesis needed for that direction. The example therefore illustrates the boundary of the equivalence without asserting either direction as new content.
